findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket (including uploaded vendor roster data) are not encrypted at rest by default.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is associated with this bucket and no ACL is explicitly set, leaving the bucket without an explicit safeguard against public exposure.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket storing ledger export data, meaning sensitive financial data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is configured to explicitly prevent public access to this sensitive ledger data bucket.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest despite versioning and logging being configured.
No public access block configuration exists to prevent this bucket from being made public.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, leaving operational runbooks (which may contain sensitive infrastructure details) unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is present to explicitly prevent public exposure of this bucket.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL (valid values include 'log-delivery-write', 'private', etc.); this appears to be a typo that will either fail or unintentionally resolve to a different, potentially permissive, access grant on a bucket that holds sensitive audit/compliance logs.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public access to this audit trail bucket, which is critical since it stores logs used for compliance and forensic purposes.
